name: Places in the Utrecht Region: Eight Pairwise Questions (Urban to Rural)
description:
Method replication: participants compare pairs of street-level photos from across the Utrecht region and answer the eight questions of the paper's Table 1 (which place is more urban, more rural, safer, more natural, more beautiful, more residential, better for outdoor recreation, better for social activities), 5 pairs per question, 40 choices in all as in the paper's maximum; the images are not the paper's stimuli (108 Google Street View images sampled at evenly spaced points over the city, villages, farmland and nature of the Utrecht region, 2020–2026).

Original study: Switalski, Van Strien & Grêt-Regamey (2025), Journal of Land Use Science 20(1), 61–81. A representative online survey of 10,042 people in the Netherlands, quota sampled by gender, age, education and region, compared Google Street View photos of 7,008 places sampled with even density across the 750 km² Utrecht urban–rural region (at most 40 comparisons each). Bradley–Terry scores for the eight perception indicators were combined with form and function indicators and clustered into place types.

Differences from the original study: (1) newly fetched Google Street View images at 108 places instead of the authors' 7,008 photos, which are not released; (2) every participant answers all eight questions with 5 pairs each, whereas the paper does not report how comparisons were spread over the questions; (3) the background questions (gender, age, education, where you live) are written for this template, without the paper's quota sampling.
author: Switalski, Van Strien & Grêt-Regamey
